_meta.purpose: Glossary seed for the app. India-specific, written for an ordinary taxpayer rather than a professional.
_meta.usage_note: These double as the chatbot's disambiguation layer. When a user types 'what is 80C', the glossary entry is the fast path; the corpus retrieval is the deep path.

terms.def: The year in which income of the preceding financial year is assessed and taxed. Income earned in FY 2025-26 is assessed in AY 2026-27. Replaced by the single concept of 'Tax Year' under the Income-tax Act, 2025, but the term survives in everyday use and in all pre-2026 records.
1 April to 31 March. The year in which you actually earn the income.
The single period concept introduced by the Income-tax Act, 2025, replacing the previous-year and assessment-year pair from 1 April 2026.
The financial year in which income is earned, under the 1961 Act terminology. Now superseded by 'Tax Year'.
The traditional tax structure with lower slab thresholds but the full range of deductions and exemptions - 80C, 80D, HRA, LTA, home loan interest and the rest. Must be actively opted into.
The default tax structure from FY 2023-24. Wider slabs and lower rates, but almost no deductions. Governed by s.115BAC of the 1961 Act, now s.202 of the 2025 Act.
The new regime. If you do nothing, you are taxed under it. The old regime requires a positive election.

The form used to opt out of the new regime. Mandatory only for taxpayers with business or professional income; salaried taxpayers simply tick the option inside the ITR. Must be filed by the original due date.
The sum of income under all five heads, after head-specific exemptions and deductions but BEFORE Chapter VI-A deductions.
Gross total income minus Chapter VI-A deductions. This is the figure your slab rate is applied to and the figure the rebate threshold is tested against.
The five categories all income must fall into: Salary; House Property; Profits and Gains of Business or Profession; Capital Gains; Income from Other Sources.

A marginal rate. Only the income falling within a band is taxed at that band's rate - moving into the 30% bracket does not tax your whole income at 30%. The most widely misunderstood concept in Indian personal tax.
The rate applied to your next rupee of income. Relevant for every 'should I invest in this' decision.
Total tax divided by total income. Always lower than the marginal rate because of the slab structure.
Income below which no tax is payable. Old regime: Rs 2.5 lakh, Rs 3 lakh (60-79), Rs 5 lakh (80+). New regime: Rs 4 lakh for everyone regardless of age.

A direct reduction in tax, not in income. Resident individuals only. New regime: up to Rs 60,000 where total income is up to Rs 12 lakh. Old regime: up to Rs 12,500 where total income is up to Rs 5 lakh. Does not apply to tax on capital gains or other special-rate income.
A cap that prevents the extra tax from crossing a threshold exceeding the extra income that crossed it. Applies to the new-regime rebate cliff at Rs 12 lakh and to every surcharge threshold.

An additional levy on the tax itself, not on income. Starts at 10% above Rs 50 lakh of total income and rises to 37% in the old regime; capped at 25% in the new regime. Capped at 15% on dividend and capital-gains income in both.
4% levied on income tax plus surcharge, after all reliefs. The final step in the computation.
A flat deduction from salary or pension requiring no proof or bills. Rs 75,000 in the new regime, Rs 50,000 in the old.

The part of the Act containing the 80-series deductions. Almost entirely unavailable in the new regime, which allows only employer NPS (80CCD(2)), Agniveer (80CCH) and additional employee cost (80JJAA).

A deduction of up to Rs 1.5 lakh for specified investments and payments - PPF, EPF, ELSS, life insurance premium, 5-year tax-saver FDs, NSC, SSY, home loan principal, children's tuition. Old regime only. Unchanged since FY 2014-15. Now s.123 read with Schedule XV.
An additional Rs 50,000 deduction for your own NPS Tier I contribution, over and above the Rs 1.5 lakh cap. Old regime only.

Deduction for your EMPLOYER'S contribution to your NPS account. Available in BOTH regimes. Capped at 14% of Basic+DA in the new regime for every employer; 10% for private employers in the old regime. The single most valuable new-regime deduction.
Health insurance premium deduction. Rs 25,000 for self and family, another Rs 25,000 for parents, rising to Rs 50,000 each where the insured are 60 or above. Maximum Rs 1 lakh. Old regime only.
80TTA: Rs 10,000 on savings account interest for those under 60. 80TTB: Rs 50,000 on savings, fixed and recurring deposit interest for senior citizens. Mutually exclusive. Old regime only.
Deduction for home loan interest. Rs 2 lakh for a self-occupied property (old regime only). Uncapped for a let-out property (both regimes, but the resulting loss is stranded in the new regime).

House Rent Allowance. Exempt to the extent of the LEAST of: actual HRA received; 50% of salary in a metro or 40% elsewhere; rent paid minus 10% of salary. Old regime only. 'Salary' here means Basic plus DA.
Leave Travel Allowance. Exempts the travel fare for two domestic journeys in a block of four calendar years. Fare only - no hotels, food or sightseeing. Old regime only.
A non-cash benefit from your employer - company car, rent-free accommodation, subsidised loan - valued under prescribed rules and ADDED to taxable salary. Applies in both regimes.

An employee whose perquisites are taxable on the wider basis - a director, someone with 20%+ voting power, or an employee whose monetary salary exceeds Rs 4 lakh (raised from Rs 50,000 by Notification 133/2025).
Adjusting a loss under one head against income under another in the same year. The new regime bars any set-off of house property loss against salary.
Taking an unabsorbed loss into future years - usually eight. Requires the return to be filed by the original due date, with narrow exceptions.
Profit on transfer of a capital asset. Taxed at special rates, not slab rates, and not covered by the s.87A rebate.
Gain on an asset held for a short period - 12 months or less for listed equity, 24 months for immovable property. Listed equity STCG is taxed at 20%; other assets at slab rates.
Gain on an asset held beyond the threshold period. Taxed at 12.5% without indexation across asset classes. Listed equity LTCG has an annual exemption of Rs 1,25,000.

Adjusting an asset's cost for inflation to reduce taxable gain. Abolished for most assets from 23 July 2024. A grandfathered option survives only for resident individuals and HUFs on land or building acquired before that date, who may pay the lower of 12.5% without indexation and 20% with it.

Protecting an existing position from a rule change. In Indian capital gains it refers both to the 31 January 2018 cost-stepping for listed equity and to the 23 July 2024 indexation option for property.
Securities Transaction Tax, levied on listed securities trades. Raised from 1 April 2026: futures 0.05% on sale, options 0.15% on premium.

Tax paid during the year rather than after it, in four instalments (15%, 45%, 75%, 100% cumulative) due 15 June, 15 September, 15 December and 15 March. Required if your net liability is Rs 10,000 or more.
Tax Deducted at Source. Tax withheld by the payer - employer, bank, tenant - and deposited against your PAN. Visible in Form 26AS and the AIS.
Tax Collected at Source. Collected by a seller on specified transactions, notably foreign remittances under the LRS and overseas tour packages.
The TDS certificate your employer issues, summarising salary paid and tax deducted. Part A is the TDS summary; Part B is the salary and deduction detail.
Your consolidated tax statement - all TDS, TCS, advance tax and self-assessment tax credited against your PAN.

Annual Information Statement. A far wider record than 26AS, covering interest, dividends, securities transactions, property deals and foreign remittances. Check it before filing; mismatches trigger notices.
Interest at 1% per month for, respectively: filing late; paying less than 90% of assessed tax as advance tax; and missing an advance tax instalment. Now ss.423, 424 and 425.
A return filed after the due date. Costs you the right to carry forward most losses and the right to opt out of the new regime for that year.
A corrected return replacing one already filed. The window was extended to 12 months from the end of the assessment year, with a nominal fee.
A return filed well after the deadline on payment of additional tax, allowing disclosure of missed income without prosecution.
Permanent Account Number. The ten-character identifier linking every tax transaction to you.
The income-tax officer with jurisdiction over your return.
A pooled vehicle investing many investors' money in securities under a professional manager, regulated by SEBI.
Net Asset Value. The per-unit value of a fund, computed daily as (assets minus liabilities) divided by units outstanding. A low NAV does not mean a cheap fund.
Systematic Investment Plan. A fixed amount invested at fixed intervals, buying more units when prices are low - rupee cost averaging.
A SIP that increases by a set percentage each year, tracking income growth. Over 10-20 years the difference against a flat SIP is dramatic.
A single one-time investment, as opposed to a SIP.
Systematic Withdrawal Plan. Regular withdrawals from a corpus. Each withdrawal is a redemption and triggers capital gains on the units sold.
Systematic Transfer Plan. Moving money gradually from one fund to another, typically from a liquid fund into equity.
The annual percentage of assets the fund charges for management, deducted from NAV. Compounds against you over decades - a 1% difference over 25 years is enormous.
A plan bought without a distributor, carrying a lower expense ratio than the regular plan of the identical fund. The difference is pure return.
A plan bought through a distributor, whose commission is embedded in a higher expense ratio.
A charge for redeeming before a stated period, commonly 1% within a year.
Equity Linked Savings Scheme. An equity fund qualifying for 80C with a three-year lock-in - the shortest of any 80C instrument. Old regime only for the tax benefit.
A fund tracking an index rather than picking stocks. Low cost, no manager risk, market returns by construction.
Exchange Traded Fund. An index fund traded on an exchange like a share, requiring a demat account.
A fund investing in bonds and money-market instruments. Units bought on or after 1 April 2023 are taxed at slab rates regardless of holding period.
A debt fund holding instruments maturing within 91 days. Used as a parking place for short-term money.
A fund holding both equity and debt. Tax treatment depends on the equity proportion - above 65% it is taxed as equity.

terms.term: Large Cap / Mid Cap / Small Cap
terms.def: SEBI's classification by market capitalisation rank: top 100 companies, 101st to 250th, and 251st onward.
Assets Under Management. The total value of assets a fund or house manages.
Asset Management Company. The entity that runs the mutual fund schemes.
Compound Annual Growth Rate. The constant annual rate that takes a starting value to an ending value. Valid only for a single lumpsum - never use it for a SIP.
Extended Internal Rate of Return. The annualised return on irregular cashflows. The only correct measure for a real portfolio with SIPs, additions and withdrawals.
Total gain as a percentage of the amount invested, ignoring time. Useless for comparing investments of different durations.
Returns measured over every possible window of a given length, rather than from one fixed start date. A far more honest picture than point-to-point returns.
The effect of investing a fixed amount regularly: you buy more units when prices fall and fewer when they rise, lowering average cost.
Earning returns on your returns. The single most important idea in personal finance, and the reason starting early matters more than investing more.
Return after inflation, computed as (1+nominal)/(1+inflation) - 1. Not simply nominal minus inflation.
Return before adjusting for inflation.
Divide 72 by the annual return to estimate the years to double your money. Rough but useful.
How you split money across equity, debt, gold and cash. Empirically the largest single driver of long-run portfolio outcomes - larger than security selection.
Restoring your target allocation by selling what has grown and buying what has lagged. Enforces selling high and buying low. Remember it triggers capital gains.
Spreading risk across uncorrelated assets. Holding eight similar equity funds is not diversification.
The degree to which returns fluctuate. Not the same thing as risk of permanent loss, though the two are often conflated.
The statistical measure of volatility - how far returns typically stray from their average.
Return above the risk-free rate per unit of volatility. Higher is better.
Sensitivity to market movements. A beta of 1.2 means the asset typically moves 20% more than the market in either direction.
Return above what the asset's beta would predict. The measure of whether a manager actually added value.
Price divided by earnings per share. How many rupees you pay for one rupee of annual profit.
Share price multiplied by shares outstanding - the market's valuation of the whole company.
A distribution of company profit to shareholders. Taxable at slab rates in the shareholder's hands since FY 2020-21, with TDS above Rs 5,000.
The account holding your securities electronically, with NSDL or CDSL.
Free additional shares issued from reserves. Your total value is unchanged; the per-share price adjusts down.
Dividing existing shares into more shares of lower face value. Cosmetic - total value is unchanged.
A company repurchasing its own shares. Reported to be taxed as capital gains rather than as dividend from FY 2026-27 - verify before relying on this.
A bank deposit at a fixed rate for a fixed term. Interest is fully taxable at slab rates and TDS applies above Rs 40,000 (Rs 50,000 for senior citizens).
A deposit built by fixed monthly instalments at a fixed rate.
The rate at which the RBI lends to commercial banks. Most floating-rate retail loans are now benchmarked to it, so a repo cut flows into your EMI.
Marginal Cost of Funds based Lending Rate. The older internal benchmark for bank loans, now largely superseded by external benchmarks.
Equated Monthly Instalment. A constant monthly payment covering both interest and principal, with the interest share highest at the start.
The schedule showing how each EMI splits between interest and principal over the loan's life.
Paying off loan principal ahead of schedule. Reducing tenure usually saves far more interest than reducing EMI.
An interest rate that moves with a benchmark. Most Indian home loans are floating.
A 300-900 score from CIBIL, Experian or Equifax summarising your credit behaviour. Drives both loan approval and the rate you are offered.
The total annualised return on a bond held to maturity, accounting for price, coupons and time remaining.
The stated interest a bond pays on its face value.
National Pension System. A market-linked, PFRDA-regulated retirement account. Tier I is the locked pension account; Tier II is a liquid add-on. At exit, a portion must buy an annuity.
The mandatory, locked-in pension account. Minimum Rs 1,000 a year. Eligible for 80CCD(1), 80CCD(1B) and 80CCD(2).
A voluntary, fully liquid investment account requiring an active Tier I. No lock-in and, for most subscribers, no tax benefit.
The NPS option where you set your own split across asset classes E, C, G and A, subject to caps.
The NPS life-cycle option where equity exposure tapers automatically with age. LC75 aggressive, LC50 moderate (the default), LC25 conservative, and the newer Balanced Life Cycle fund.
A contract paying a regular income for life in exchange for a lump sum. NPS requires a minimum portion of the corpus to be annuitised at exit. Annuity income is fully taxable at slab rates.
Unified Pension Scheme. An assured-pension option offered to central government employees as an alternative to NPS. The window to opt closed on 30 November 2025.

Atal Pension Yojana. A government-guaranteed small pension scheme with fixed pension slabs from Rs 1,000 to Rs 5,000 a month. Anyone who is or has been an income-tax payer has been barred from joining since 1 October 2022.
Employees' Provident Fund. Mandatory retirement savings for covered employees - 12% from the employee, matched by the employer, on a wage ceiling of Rs 15,000. Rate declared annually by the CBT.
Voluntary Provident Fund. Additional employee contribution to EPF beyond the mandatory 12%, at the same rate of return. Interest on employee contributions above Rs 2.5 lakh a year is taxable.
Employees' Pension Scheme. The pension component carved out of the employer's EPF contribution.
A lump sum payable on leaving after five years of service. Exempt up to Rs 20 lakh over a lifetime for non-government employees, fully exempt for government employees.
Payment for unused leave. On retirement it is exempt up to Rs 25 lakh over a lifetime for non-government employees. Encashment DURING service is fully taxable.
Taking part of your pension as a lump sum instead of monthly income. Fully exempt for government employees; one-third or one-half exempt for others depending on whether gratuity was also received.
An employer-run retirement fund. Employer contributions to PF, superannuation and NPS combined above Rs 7.5 lakh a year become a taxable perquisite.
Public Provident Fund. A 15-year government savings scheme, extendable in five-year blocks. Currently 7.10%. Fully tax-free at contribution, accrual and maturity - the classic EEE instrument.
Exempt-Exempt-Exempt. Contribution, accrual and withdrawal are all tax-free. PPF and SSY qualify.
Exempt-Exempt-Taxed. Tax relief going in and while growing, but taxed on withdrawal.
Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana. A scheme for a girl child under 10, currently 8.20%, with deposits for 15 years and maturity at 21. Tax-free throughout.
Senior Citizens Savings Scheme. A five-year scheme for those 60 and above, currently 8.20%, paid quarterly. Interest is fully taxable.
National Savings Certificate. A five-year instrument currently at 7.70%, compounded annually and paid at maturity. Qualifies for 80C, and the accrued interest re-qualifies each year.
Kisan Vikas Patra. Doubles your money over 115 months at the current 7.50%. No tax benefit; interest is fully taxable.
Post Office Monthly Income Scheme. A five-year deposit paying monthly interest, currently 7.40%. Fully taxable.

A government bond denominated in grams of gold, paying 2.5% interest on top of gold price movement. Discontinued for new issues after February 2024. Capital gains on redemption at maturity were exempt for original subscribers.
Pure life cover with no maturity value. The cheapest and most efficient way to protect dependants. Premium qualifies for 80C in the old regime.
A policy mixing insurance with savings. Typically delivers poor returns on both counts compared with term insurance plus a separate investment.
Unit Linked Insurance Plan. Market-linked investment wrapped in an insurance policy, with a five-year lock-in. Maturity proceeds are taxable where the annual premium exceeds Rs 2.5 lakh.
The exemption for life insurance maturity proceeds. Restricted for policies issued on or after 1 April 2023 where annual premium exceeds Rs 5 lakh - those proceeds are taxed at slab rates.
The amount the insurer pays on the insured event.
An optional add-on to a policy, such as critical illness or accidental death cover.
A house you live in. It generates no rental income, and its home loan interest is deductible up to Rs 2 lakh - old regime only.
A rented property. Rent is taxable, 30% of net annual value is deductible as a standard deduction, and home loan interest is deductible without limit in both regimes.
Rent received or reasonably expected, less municipal taxes actually paid. The starting point for house property income.
A property treated as rented for tax even if vacant. From FY 2024-25 a taxpayer may treat up to two houses as self-occupied, so the concept now bites only from the third property onward.
The government's assessed value of a property. Used as a floor for capital gains where the sale price is lower, and it determines eligibility for several deductions.
The minimum government-notified rate per unit area for registering a property in a locality.
Three to six months of expenses in liquid, accessible form. The first thing to build, before any investment.
Everything you own minus everything you owe.
How quickly an asset converts to cash without losing value. Real estate is illiquid; a liquid fund is not.
The minimum period before you can withdraw. ELSS three years, ULIP five, PPF fifteen, NPS until exit conditions are met.
The rate at which money loses purchasing power. Any return below inflation is a real loss, however positive the number looks.
